Orange Cat Project · Night Report

The Guest House

Night of 09-01/02: the stray got in twice — and both unseen moments fell inside a blind spot the system creates for itself after every fire.

2026-09-02 · patrol.log, two fire videos, and the first silent exit capture · tripwire night 1 of 5 · corrected per Dave: both events were entries

Two entries, and the blind spot that hid both. The stray dove through the flap at 04:37:02, two seconds after the drill. It came back out shortly after (the 04:38:03 motion event, scored as an unidentified animal, was almost certainly this) — then returned at 04:51:03, took a drill mid-approach, dodged aside, and went straight back in through the flap — a resident tuxedo strolled into view a few seconds later — then had its ~9-minute meal before its clean exit at 05:01:54. Both of the moments nobody saw — the first exit and the second entry — happened while the patrol was blocked for ~75 seconds recording video of its own fire. The camera kept filming; the judge left the room. That flaw is now fix #1.

The tripwire opened its account: this counts as an entry night — 1 of the 2 allowed, night 1 of 5.

The night, in order

21:45:19
Stream hot in 4s. One ~30s stall at 00:33 — the same minute as the night before; something scheduled on Dima's side (question 2).
–00:06
Quiet: three resident sightings, zero orange.
04:36:56
First glimpse, distant and low-confidence. Engaged in 3s flat (the new first-glimpse rule working) — drill at :59 — but the cat sprinted and dove through the flap at 04:37:02. The 17-second cat-fight scream played to its tail.entry 1
~04:38
Back out almost immediately — unseen: the patrol was blocked in its post-fire video capture. The server's 04:38:03 motion event (animal, not scored orange) is the exit's only trace.
04:51:03
Second approach, from the right. Drill at :06, dodged aside — then, with the patrol blind in its post-fire capture until 04:52:20, it went straight in through the flap. Several seconds later a resident tuxedo strolled into view, entirely unimpressed.entry 2
05:01:54
Exit after the ~9-minute meal. Held mid-opening, classified exiting, zero sounds — and captured by the new silent recorder, whose pre-roll is what proved the direction and untangled the night.silent

Questions

  1. What runs at 00:33? The stream stalled ~30s at 00:33:14 and 00:33:37 on consecutive nights — that's a schedule, not chance (HA nightly backup? Protect maintenance?). A predictable degraded window in cat hours is worth closing.
  2. Were the sounds audible indoors? Two drills and two 17-second cat-fight screams played 04:36–04:52.
  3. Does tonight settle the close-range argument? Three dive-throughs in three nights (01:58, 04:37, and the 04:51 feint-and-enter) against four mid-patio repels. Sound owns the open patio and keeps losing the doorstep. The physical obstacle (R4) and the tripwire are where that argument now lives — and tonight also showed the cat will absorb a drill, retreat ten meters, and simply wait us out.

Fixes queued for daylight

  • #1 — thread the fired-path video capture. It blocks the patrol for ~75s after every fire; both of tonight's unseen transitions happened inside those windows, and the same blackout hid the 01:58 dive's aftermath yesterday. After this fix the patrol never stops judging.
  • play_media timeout 10s → 25s: it blocks until playback ends, so both 17-second screams were logged "failed" while almost certainly playing. The 12s far opener would hit the same false failure — and the false failure also killed the rest of both rapid ladders.
  • Trim the cat-fight scream to ~8s — the top rung doesn't need 17 seconds of 4am screaming to make its point.
  • Flip DETER_SOUND_BASE when Dima stages the sound pack (not yet detected).

Epilogue — the alternative

An alternative, of course, is to welcome the orange cat into your home. The case for it was made some eight centuries ago by Rumi — the 13th-century Persian poet and Sufi mystic — in his poem The Guest House:

This being human is a guest house.
Every morning a new arrival.
A joy, a depression, a meanness,
some momentary awareness comes
as an unexpected visitor.

Welcome and entertain them all!
Even if they’re a crowd of sorrows,
who violently sweep your house
empty of its furniture,
still, treat each guest honorably.
He may be clearing you out
for some new delight.

The dark thought, the shame, the malice,
meet them at the door laughing,
and invite them in.

Be grateful for whoever comes,
because each has been sent
as a guide from beyond.

—Rumi, translated by Coleman Barks
